title: Foreground Sampling and Spatial Support in Pavement Crack Segmentation
mechanism: Controlled study at 2 px tolerance AP: crack-biased crop sampling hurts because it makes background area unreachable; GroupNorm instead of BatchNorm lifts a random-crop U-Net.
adaptation: (a) Swap every decoder BatchNorm2d in U-Net++ for GroupNorm(16) while the pretrained encoder keeps BN, batch 8 of mixed sources. (b) Any crack/inactive oversampling or cropping we add must keep the whole cell reachable. Their paired-seed, prespecified-contrast protocol with a practical floor is a template for the benchmark.
min_experiment: Arm: PF with GroupNorm decoder, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: test clean crack relF1@2, crack IoU, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill: crack relF1@2 and inactive IoU both within 0.012 of PF.
evidence: R (full text): Crack500 full-res, U-Net from scratch, AdamW 3e-4, 20k updates, batch 16, BCE+Dice, flips+rot90, 3 paired seeds. AP2 random crops 0.812 (BN), positive-only 0.789, 10% positive 0.730; positive-only made 47% of area unreachable. GroupNorm random 0.844 vs BN 0.812 (+0.032).
prior_overlap: none; normalisation and sampling never varied here.
